//: The browser half of the console — the code `vite build` bundles into the served assets. It is referenced from the solution-style tsconfig.json, so an editor uses it, and that is currently the only thing that does: `build` is `vite build && tsup && tsc -p tsconfig.react.json`, and vite transpiles through esbuild, which typechecks nothing. So src/client/** is shipped browser code that no command in this repo has ever typechecked.
//not-in-the-gate: Deliberately NOT run by `pnpm typecheck`, and this note exists so that stays a decision rather than an oversight. It does not pass, and it never has. On a clean tree it reports five errors, every one of them TS2375/TS2379 under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` — three in App.tsx passing `T | undefined` into a React prop typed `T`, two in transport.ts doing the same into its own fetch wrapper. They are NOT stale-artefact errors: they survive a fresh `pnpm build`. The cause is that this config extends ../../tsconfig.base.json while the code beneath it has only ever been compiled by esbuild, and while packages/react — whose props three of them cross — does not set that flag in its own build config, so those prop types were written without it.
//how-it-gets-fixed: Fix the five, then add this config to scripts/typecheck-specs.mjs, or give the package a second `typecheck` entry. Fix rather than delete: this is the only config covering src/client/**, so deleting it leaves the console's whole browser bundle typechecked by nothing, which is worse than a config that is honestly red. What must NOT happen is switching `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` off here to make it green — two of the five are the dashboard's own code violating the dashboard's own base config, and that is a real defect rather than a cross-package strictness mismatch. (The spec config next door does turn it off, for the narrower reason spelled out there: it pulls packages/react SOURCE into its program, and cannot hold another package's code to options its owner never applied.)
//include: `src/app/**` was in this list and matches nothing — there is no src/app, and no sign there ever was. Dropped, because a glob over a directory that does not exist reads like coverage.
